result.markdown: --- title: "Session 2 — Cluster-Robust Standard Errors and GEE" subtitle: "Sandwich variance · few clusters (CR2) · generalised estimating equations · working correlation · Lab 2" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Session 1: clusters make the naive **SE too small** (design effect 2.4) - Today: two ways to **keep the model and fix the SE** - By the end you can: - compute **cluster-robust** standard errors - fit a **GEE** and choose a **working correlation** - read a GEE odds ratio as a **population-averaged** effect - know when robust methods are **unreliable** (few clusters) ::: # Topic 1 — Cluster-robust SEs {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Same model, honest SE ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_lm <- lm(sbp ~ arm + age + sex + bmi, data = bp12) rbind(naive = summary(m_lm)$coefficients["armProgramme", 1:2], cluster_robust = coeftest(m_lm, vcov = vcovCL(m_lm, cluster = bp12$village))["armProgramme", 1:2]) |> round(3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Estimate Std. Error naive -3.424 1.151 cluster_robust -3.424 1.593 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} The **estimate does not change**. The **standard error** grows from **1.15 to 1.59** (about 40% larger), because the sandwich estimator uses the **actual variability between villages** instead of assuming independence. ::: ## How it works (idea only) ::: {.incremental} - Fit the usual model; keep the **coefficients** - For the **variance**, add up the residuals **within each cluster** before squaring: correlation inside a cluster is then **captured**, whatever its form - No assumption about **why** or **how** observations are correlated - Works for `lm`, `glm` and many other models: `vcovCL(model, cluster = ...)` ::: ::: {.warn} It needs **enough clusters**. With about **fewer than 40**, the robust SE tends to be **too small**, and with fewer than about 10 it is unreliable. ::: ## Few clusters: the CR2 correction ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} coef_test(m_lm, vcov = "CR2", cluster = bp12$village)["armProgramme", ] ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Alternative hypothesis: two-sided Coef. Estimate SE Null value t-stat d.f. (Satt) p-val (Satt) Sig. armProgramme -3.42 1.62 0 -2.12 37.4 0.0407 * ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - `clubSandwich` gives a **small-sample correction** (CR2) and **Satterthwaite degrees of freedom** (about **37** here) - SE 1.62 vs 1.59 and a **t-test** instead of a z-test: a more honest p-value - With 40 villages the difference is small; with 15 it can be large ::: # Topic 2 — GEE {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Generalised estimating equations ::: {.incremental} - Fit a **population-averaged** (marginal) model: *what is the average difference between arms?* - Choose a **working correlation** for observations in a cluster: `independence`, `exchangeable`, `ar1`, `unstructured` - Use **robust (sandwich) SEs** so inference stays valid **even if the working correlation is wrong** - `geepack::geeglm()`: data **sorted by cluster id**, and no missing values in the model variables ::: ## A GEE for SBP ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} d12 <- bp12 |> arrange(village) g1 <- geeglm(sbp ~ arm + age + sex + bmi, id = village, data = d12, family = gaussian, corstr = "exchangeable") round(summary(g1)$coefficients["armProgramme", ], 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Estimate Std.err Wald Pr(>|W|) armProgramme -3.562 1.544 5.324 0.021 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} summary(g1)$corr ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Estimate Std.err alpha 0.05789055 0.02183997 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} The estimate is about **−3.6 mmHg** with a robust SE of about **1.5**. The **alpha** (≈ 0.06) is the estimated within-village correlation, in line with the ICC. ::: ## Working correlation: does the choice matter? ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g_ind <- geeglm(sbp ~ arm + age + sex + bmi, id = village, data = d12, family = gaussian, corstr = "independence") c(independence = coef(g_ind)[["armProgramme"]], exchangeable = coef(g1)[["armProgramme"]]) |> round(2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` independence exchangeable -3.42 -3.56 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - Both are **valid** with robust SEs - A **good** working correlation gives **narrower CIs** (more efficient) - For a **cluster-level** exposure the choice matters little - Use **exchangeable** for clusters, **ar1** for equally spaced repeated measures ::: ## A binary outcome: controlled BP ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} g2 <- geeglm(controlled ~ arm + age + sex + bmi, id = village, data = d12, family = binomial, corstr = "exchangeable") round(exp(cbind(OR = coef(g2), confint.default(g2)))["armProgramme", ], 2) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` OR 2.5 % 97.5 % 1.21 0.73 2.00 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} OR **1.2** (95% CI **0.7 to 2.0**): the interval includes 1, so there is **no clear evidence** of an effect on **controlled BP** (SBP below 140) at 12 months. It is the **population-averaged** odds ratio: the odds in the average person of one arm compared with the other. ::: ## Cluster-robust lm or GEE? | | Cluster-robust `lm`/`glm` | GEE | |---|---|---| | Correlation | ignored in the estimate, fixed in the SE | modelled (working correlation) | | Estimate | the independence one | can be more **efficient** | | Repeated measures | not designed for it | yes (`waves`, `ar1`) | | Interpretation | marginal | **marginal** | | Few clusters | use **CR2** | use small-sample corrections | ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 2 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `clustered-workshop/labs/lab2_gee.R` - cluster-robust SEs with `vcovCL` - `geeglm` with exchangeable and independence - a binary GEE and the CR2 correction ::: **Time:** 40 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c2q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="yv2ag2.2bm2r0" data-show="VGhlIHN0YW5kYXJkIGVycm9yIGNoYW5nZXM7IHRoZSBjb2VmZmljaWVudCBzdGF5cyB0aGUg c2FtZQ==" data-explain="QSBjbHVzdGVyLXJvYnVzdCAoc2FuZHdpY2gpIFNFIG9ubHkgcmVwbGFjZXMgdGhlIHZhcmlh bmNlIGVzdGltYXRlLiBUaGUgY29lZmZpY2llbnRzIGFyZSB0aG9zZSBvZiB0aGUgb3JkaW5h cnkgbW9kZWwu"} What changes when you replace the naive SE by a cluster-robust SE in the same linear model? - The coefficient and the standard error are both recomputed from the data - The p-value changes, while the confidence interval keeps the same width - The model is refitted with a random intercept for each cluster - The standard error changes; the coefficient stays the same ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c2q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="yv2noo.2bmh8a" data-show="VGhlIHNhbmR3aWNoIHZhcmlhbmNlIHJlbGllcyBvbiBtYW55IGNsdXN0ZXJzLCBhbmQgMTIg aXMgdG9vIGZldw==" data-explain="VGhlIHNhbmR3aWNoIHZhcmlhbmNlIGlzIGVzdGltYXRlZCBmcm9tIHRoZSBjbHVzdGVycy4g V2l0aCBmZXcgY2x1c3RlcnMgaXQgaXMgYmlhc2VkIGRvd253YXJkcywgc28gdXNlIHNtYWxs LXNhbXBsZSBjb3JyZWN0aW9ucyBsaWtlIENSMiBvciBhIGNsdXN0ZXItbGV2ZWwgYW5hbHlz aXMu"} A trial has 12 villages. Why is a standard cluster-robust SE not reliable here? - The sandwich variance relies on many clusters, and 12 is too few - Cluster-robust SEs are defined for binary outcomes and cannot be used for SBP - Villages need to have the same number of people for the method to work - The method requires measurements from at least four visits per person ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c2q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="yv30xe.2bmvpo" data-show="YSBwb3B1bGF0aW9uLWF2ZXJhZ2VkIGVmZmVjdCBiZXR3ZWVuIHRoZSB0d28gYXJtcw==" data-explain="R0VFIG1vZGVscyB0aGUgYXZlcmFnZSBvdXRjb21lIGluIGVhY2ggYXJtIGFjcm9zcyB0aGUg cG9wdWxhdGlvbi4gVGhlIHJvYnVzdCBTRSBrZWVwcyBpbmZlcmVuY2UgdmFsaWQgZXZlbiBp ZiB0aGUgd29ya2luZyBjb3JyZWxhdGlvbiBpcyB3cm9uZy4="} In a GEE with an exchangeable working correlation, the odds ratio for the arm is best described as... - the effect for one particular village in the trial - a population-averaged effect between the two arms - the effect holding the village random effect constant - an effect that holds only when the correlation is exchangeable ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c2q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="yv3e65.2bna73" data-show="SXQgY2FuIGltcHJvdmUgZWZmaWNpZW5jeSwgYW5kIGluZmVyZW5jZSBzdGF5cyB2YWxpZCBp ZiBpdCBpcyB3cm9uZw==" data-explain="QSBnb29kIHdvcmtpbmcgc3RydWN0dXJlIGdpdmVzIG5hcnJvd2VyIGludGVydmFscy4gQmVj YXVzZSB0aGUgU0UgaXMgcm9idXN0LCBhIG1pc3NwZWNpZmllZCBzdHJ1Y3R1cmUgY29zdHMg ZWZmaWNpZW5jeSBidXQgZG9lcyBub3QgaW52YWxpZGF0ZSB0aGUgQ0ku"} What is the role of the working correlation in a GEE? - It decides whether the coefficients are biased, so it needs to be right - It is the true correlation, which has to be known before the model is fitted - It switches off the robust variance and uses the model-based one instead - It can improve efficiency, and inference stays valid if it is wrong ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c2q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="yv3rer.2bnood" data-show="Um93cyBzb3J0ZWQgYnkgdGhlIGNsdXN0ZXIgaWQsIHdpdGggbm8gbWlzc2luZyB2YWx1ZXMg aW4gdGhlIG1vZGVsIHZhcmlhYmxlcw==" data-explain="Z2VlZ2xtIGFzc3VtZXMgdGhhdCBvYnNlcnZhdGlvbnMgb2YgYSBjbHVzdGVyIGFyZSBjb250 aWd1b3VzIGFuZCBpdCBkb2VzIG5vdCBoYW5kbGUgbWlzc2luZyB2YWx1ZXMgaW4gdGhlIG1v ZGVsIHZhcmlhYmxlcywgc28gc29ydCBmaXJzdCBhbmQgZHJvcCBpbmNvbXBsZXRlIHJvd3Mu "} Which data preparation does geeglm need? - Rows sorted by the cluster id, with no missing values in the model variables - Rows sorted by the outcome value, keeping a single summary row for each village - One column for each visit, with the data reshaped into wide format beforehand - Complete villages, with the same number of adults in each of the villages ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Cluster-robust SE**: same estimate, honest SE (`vcovCL`) - **CR2** for fewer than about 40 clusters - **GEE**: population-averaged effect, working correlation, robust SE - **Exchangeable** for clusters, **ar1** for ordered repeated measures - Data sorted by cluster, no missing values in the model ::: **Next:** Session 3: random-intercept (mixed) models

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
